title: Medial tibial stress syndrome: conservative treatment options
claims: In the subacute phase, decreasing weekly running distance, frequency and intensity by about 50% can improve symptoms without complete cessation of activity.
Low-impact cross-training alternatives listed for rehabilitation include pool running, swimming, an elliptical machine and a stationary bicycle.

Return to activity should be step-wise: over weeks, athletes slowly increase training intensity and duration and add sport-specific activities, jumping exercises and hill running only while remaining pain-free.
Athletes should scale back any exercise that exacerbates their symptoms or causes pain.
Most medial tibial stress syndrome treatment recommendations rest on expert opinion and clinical experience, with a general paucity of randomized controlled trials.
